subject: Cannot reproduce SEM results in two splitted samples

messages.author: d08549370f34b232
messages.subject: Cannot reproduce SEM results in two splitted samples
parts:
Hi all,

I have a very large sample size (n > 5000) and a very complicated model (df = 232). I randomly split the sample into two and test the model on both. Both have pretty good measurement indices but the significance tests for about 3 variables' regression coefficient contradict between the two samples. I wonder if this means my data doesn't fit the model well, or I can report the other consistent results and call for more research on the three variables. 

My second question is: I was playing with the models by adding/removing variables. That changes the significance test of other variables' regression coefficient (from sig to not sig or vice versa). Is it normal or does it imply some data assumption violations? 

Thank you in advance!
~ K

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Cannot reproduce SEM results in two splitted samples
parts: but the significance tests for about 3 variables' regression coefficient contradict between the two samples. I wonder if this means my data doesn't fit the model well, or I can report the other consistent results and call for more research on the three variables.

Isn't that the whole point of doing cross-validation?  This isn't a lavaan questions, so you can ask for more advice on SEMNET, but split-sample cross-validation is not recommended because different split samples will give you different cross-validation results, due to Monte Carlo error.

http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html
